examples.japanese: {地方|ちほう}の{料理|りょうり}
{関東|かんとう}{地方|ちほう}は{雨|あめ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: The Kanto region gets a lot of rain.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{地方|ちほう}によって{方言|ほうげん}が{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: Dialects differ depending on the region of Japan.

examples.japanese: {地方|ちほう}から{東京|とうきょう}に{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: I came to Tokyo from the countryside.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{人|ひと}が{地方|ちほう}を{離|はな}れて{都会|とかい}に{出|で}るため、{地方|ちほう}の{人口|じんこう}が{減|へ}っている。
examples.english: Because young people leave the countryside for the city, the population in rural areas is declining.

notes:
{地方|ちほう} has two main uses: a geographical region or the provinces/rural areas (as opposed to major cities like Tokyo).

MEANINGS:
1. Region/district: {関東|かんとう}{地方|ちほう} (Kanto region)
2. Rural areas/provinces: {地方|ちほう}に{住|す}む (to live in the countryside)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {地方|ちほう}{都市|とし}: regional city
- {地方|ちほう}{自治体|じちたい}: local government
- {地方|ちほう}{公務員|こうむいん}: local government employee
- {地方|ちほう}{税|ぜい}: local tax

CONTRAST:
- {地方|ちほう}: region; rural areas
- {都会|とかい}: city, urban area
- {田舎|いなか}: countryside (more casual/intimate)
